summary.summary:
## Background
This case–control study in Iraqi patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) assessed whether variants in inflammasome-related genes CARD8 (rs2043211 A>T; p.C10X) and NLRP3 (rs4612666 C>T) are associated with disease activity and response to anti–TNF-α therapy (etanercept or infliximab). One hundred RA patients and 100 controls were genotyped; serum TNF-α and IL-1β were measured, and treatment response was evaluated after 3 months.

## Key Findings
- No RA susceptibility signal: Genotype and allele frequencies for CARD8 rs2043211 and NLRP3 rs4612666 did not differ between RA patients and controls (CARD8 P=0.17/0.059; NLRP3 P=0.08/0.879).
- Cytokines track disease and response: Higher TNF-α and IL-1β correlated with higher DAS-28 (r^2=0.45 and 0.51; both P<0.0001). Non-responders had markedly elevated TNF-α (13.68 vs 4.83 pg/mL) and IL-1β (3.36 vs 1.57 pg/mL) versus responders (both P<0.0001).
- CARD8 rs2043211 (A>T):
  - T-allele carriers (AT/TT), especially TT, showed higher DAS-28 and were overrepresented among non-responders (genotype–response P<0.0001).
  - TT genotype had the highest TNF-α and IL-1β levels (both P<0.0001).
- NLRP3 rs4612666 (C>T):
  - T-allele carriers (CT/TT), especially TT, had higher DAS-28 and lower response rates to anti–TNF-α (genotype–response P<0.0001).
  - TT genotype showed the highest TNF-α and IL-1β levels (both P<0.0001).
- Drug-specific effects were similar between etanercept and infliximab; differences in cytokines or DAS-28 between the two agents were not significant.

## Clinical Implications
- T-allele carriage at CARD8 rs2043211 and NLRP3 rs4612666 identifies RA patients at higher risk of elevated inflammatory cytokines, higher disease activity, and poorer short-term response to anti–TNF-α therapy.
- Measuring baseline/early on-treatment TNF-α and IL-1β may help flag likely non-responders and guide earlier treatment adjustments.
- While these findings support the potential of CARD8 and NLRP3 genotyping to refine anti–TNF-α treatment selection, validation in larger, multi-ethnic cohorts and over longer follow-up is needed before routine clinical implementation.
